correctness.rationale: For w=0^a1^b0^c1^d with positive run lengths, Lemma 14 in Baranwal et al. forces antisquare factors to have 2 or 3 runs; the four distinct shape families count R=max(min(a,b),min(c,d)), S=min(b,c), U=max(0,min(a,b-1)-max(1,b-c)+1), V=max(0,min(b,c-1)-max(1,c-d)+1). Each three-run factor necessarily exhausts its central run. Charging R+U or R+V to the corresponding pair of runs proves <=n-1 and forces exactly the two stated equality families; supplied explicit witnesses cover n>=6. Uniform composition lattice averages converge to a Lipschitz simplex integral with O(1) total mean error; independent exponential-integral computation gives 7/16. Independently enumerated actual distinct factor strings for all 2401 positive quadruples with sides <=7, checked exact formula/equality and maxima through n=39. The infinite result follows from the run decomposition and integral, not finite checks.
residual_risks: Computer enumeration is finite; the uniform averaging proof relies on the standard simplex lattice approximation.
